markdown_content: ## Introduction to CloFab and ZFab Kit Integration This section explains the new CloFab feature introduced in Clo 2025.1 and its integration with the ZFab kit. CloFab is accessible via multiple entry points in Clo's interface, including the object browser button, fabric menu, and fabric properties. It streamlines fabric creation by combining seamless texture mapping and physical fabric property editing into one tool. CloFab connects with the ZFab kit for enhanced fabric scanning and management, offering preorder options and detailed manuals for user guidance. --- ## Accessing and Navigating the CloFab Interface CloFab creates a new fabric entry in the object browser and opens a dedicated CloFab window. Users can input fabric metadata such as fabric name, supplier, and owner in the property editor. The interface is divided into two main sections: - **Maps:** For importing and editing seamless texture maps. - **Physical Properties:** For defining fabric physical characteristics. Both sections work together to achieve a comprehensive fabric definition. --- ## Importing and Managing Fabric Maps Users import fabric maps by naming their texture files with consistent conventions, using either full or abbreviated terms (e.g., "color," "displacement," "normal map," "roughness"). Proper naming triggers automatic loading of all related maps when one is selected. After importing, users can crop the images to remove unwanted space and focus on a clean repeat unit. This is essential to avoid visual artifacts in tiling. --- ## Creating Pattern Repeats and Pattern Types Once maps are imported, users select an area to define the fabric repeat pattern. CloFab prompts users to choose a pattern type from the following options: - **Plain/Irregular:** No repeat or irregular patterns. - **Repeat:** Regular, even repeats such as stone patterns. Selecting the appropriate pattern type allows CloFab's tiling algorithm (e.g., "Tiling Auto") to automatically identify optimal repeat boundaries. Users should verify that all texture maps (color, normal, displacement, roughness, opacity) align well within the selected repeat. --- ## Saving and Exporting Fabric Maps After defining the repeat and confirming map alignment, users apply changes to generate the fabric preview. They can save all related texture maps together or individually for external use. This step finalizes the visual aspect of the fabric. --- ## Defining Physical Fabric Properties Physical properties define how the fabric behaves in simulations. Users specify: - **Fabric Type:** e.g., plain weave. - **Composition:** e.g., cotton/spandex blend. - **Weights and Dimensions:** Including fabric weight (grams per square meter) and width (e.g., 500 mm). - **Custom Numeric Inputs:** Such as thickness and other advanced parameters. Real-time simulation feedback allows users to observe drape and movement changes as they adjust these values. --- ## Advanced Physical Property Adjustments and Simulation Controls For experienced users, CloFab offers sliders to fine-tune advanced properties influencing draping and fabric stiffness. A reset option is available for reverting all changes but does not support individual parameter resets yet. Users can lock camera views or change viewing modes (e.g., square, cape, cylinder) for detailed simulation inspections. The 3D environment allows free navigation to observe fabric behavior under various conditions. --- ## Fabric Map Selection Without Custom Maps If users lack custom texture maps, CloFab provides preset fabric maps that can be applied with a single click. Users can toggle between these presets and their original maps, facilitating quick experimentation. --- ## Working with Multiple Fabrics and Pattern Adjustments CloFab supports creating multiple fabric entries simultaneously. When working with irregular patterns, users may need to manually adjust repeats by disabling auto mode and repositioning the selected area to minimize visual breaks. This manual control helps achieve precise alignment for complex or irregular patterns that automated tiling may not perfectly handle. --- ## Creating Knit Fabrics and Alternative Fabric Types Users can create knit fabrics by selecting appropriate fabric types (e.g., jersey) and compositions (e.g., cotton/polyester/spandex blends). Adjusting thickness, weight, and other physical parameters allows simulation of diverse fabric behaviors. The interface dynamically updates fabric names and properties as changes are made, ensuring fabric management remains organized. --- ## Simulation Performance and GPU Acceleration CloFab supports GPU acceleration for faster fabric simulation. Switching to GPU mode enhances performance and allows smoother observation of drape and deformation changes in real time. --- ## Applying Fabrics to Garments and Finalizing Once a fabric is defined and saved, users can apply it directly to garments within Clo. The fabric's visual and physical properties update automatically on the garment, enabling immediate simulation feedback. Multiple fabrics can be managed and applied to different garment parts, supporting complex design workflows. --- ## Summary CloFab in Clo 2025.1 combines seamless texture mapping and physical fabric property editing into one user-friendly tool integrated with the ZFab kit. It supports: - Importing and managing fabric texture maps with consistent naming conventions. - Defining and adjusting pattern repeats with automatic and manual controls. - Setting detailed physical properties including fabric type, composition, weight, and thickness. - Real-time simulation monitoring with camera locking and 3D navigation. - Handling multiple fabrics and irregular patterns. - GPU-accelerated simulations for enhanced performance. - Direct application of fabrics to garments with instant visual and physical feedback. This makes CloFab a comprehensive solution for digital fabric creation and simulation within Clo Virtual Fashion.
